## 10: PL Semantics, Evaluating wffs

::: {.r-fit-text}

(a) Suppose we are working in a PL language where ‘P’ means Fred is a fool; ‘Q’ means Fred
knows some logic; ‘R’ means Fred is a rocket scientist. Translate the following sentences into this formal language as best you can. What do you think is lost in the translations, if you can only use the ‘colourless’ connectives ‘∧’, ‘∨’ and ‘¬’?

(1) Even Fred is a rocket scientist. R
(2) Fred is a rocket scientist, but he knows no logic. (R ∧ ¬Q)
(3) Fred is a rocket scientist, moreover he knows some logic. (R ∧ Q)
(4) Fred’s a fool, even though he knows some logic. (P ∧ Q)
(5) Although Fred’s a rocket scientist, he’s a fool and even knows no logic. (R ∧ (P ∧ ¬Q))
(6) Fred’s a fool, yet he’s a rocket scientist who knows some logic. (P ∧ (R ∧ Q))
(7) Fred is a fool despite the fact that he knows some logic. (P ∧ Q)
(8) Fred is not a rocket scientist who knows some logic. ¬(R ∧ Q)
(9) Fred knows some logic unless he is a fool. (Q ∨ P) (?)

:::
